So let me start with talking about what are data. What do I think data are?
So data are the result of an observation or measurement.
They are written down, recorded. They can be text, they can be numbers.
They can be a video or an audio recording.
They're almost always a sample of something.
So it's true that if you take a herbarium specimen of an individual, you have the

And data, really key distinction. Data are intended to represent the truth.
They may be a sample, but from them, we want to know,
is something present or absent? What's its size? What condition it is in?
What's its identity or species? What relationships are there to other things?
So data are not just random recordings of information.
They are intended to represent the truth, and so that's a difference between data
and any piece of information that you might have out there.
From an ontological perspective, a widely used ontology within the biosciences is
the Information Artifact Ontology.
And so IAO defines data as a data entity, which is
an information content entity that is intended to be one or more truthful
statements about something, modulo measure imprecision or other systematic errors,
and is constructed, acquired, and acquired by a method which reliably tends
to produce approximately truthful statements.
So you can see that my perspective about what data is, it aligns very closely with
the Information Artifact Ontology.
And so in that ontology, data entity is a subclass of information
content entity, which is defined as a generically independent continuant that is
about something. I won't go into the definition of a generically independent
continuant.
But you can see that information is largely larger, a category of things
that are described, and data entity is a very specific
subtype of an information content entity.
